attributes.date: RR 189 — fourteen years before the present
attributes.eleven_days: the speed is the point — the Wardenry had a Third Rank on site inside eleven days, forty miles out. The centre is eight hundred.
attributes.outcome: ground sealed under the Fourth Article, shaft capped with plain-salt and mortar, compensation paid at the last assessed price of salt
attributes.status: the seal is still in force. No survey has ever begun. Ferrant died in RR 197.
attributes.what_ferrant_did_not_have: a crossing licence for the ground he was standing on, and therefore no season clock to force. He could only take the money. This is the single difference between Ferrant and Ysoly Tamm.
attributes.what_was_found: water at ninety feet, forty miles onto the plain. Brackish, according to the Wardenry's own survey, which no one else was ever permitted to check.
attributes.who: Ferrant, a rim merchant. The declaring Warden's name is on the roll at Bell Harrow and can be looked up by anyone who asks.
attributes.why_it_matters: it is the working precedent — the exact shape of what the Wardenry will do at the centre, already done once, cleanly, and never challenged. Everyone who is about to argue about the Fourth Article is really arguing about Ferrant.

name: The Ferrant Sinking
summary: A rim merchant named Ferrant sank a shaft forty miles onto the plain, hit water at ninety feet, and had a Warden of the Third Rank standing on his spoil-heap inside eleven days. The ground was declared a hazard, the shaft was capped with plain-salt and mortar, and Ferrant was paid the worth of forty miles of crust at the assessed salt price — enough to keep him quiet, not enough to make him rich. The seal has never been lifted and the survey it promised has never been begun.
